ranking.note: Raised: supported-platform failure of the bitcoin wrapper on Windows (exit codes lost, functional tests disabled) and a prerequisite for #36190 — on par with the other wrapper bug fix.
Raised: wrapper is outright unusable on distributions with non-default install layouts (issue #35785), a real deployment breakage rather than a nicety.
Raised: replaces a subsystem with documented privacy/deanonymization leaks and ships the standalone broadcast tool; durable value well above the ordinary new-tool P3s.
Raised and moved up: measurable snapshot-load speedup plus the txoutsetsummary tool, and it is the base for #35054 UTXO set sharing — unblocking work outranks the single-user tools below it.
Raised from P4 and moved up: silently swallowed trailing options (e.g. -rpcwallet routing to the wrong wallet) is a user-facing CLI bug, not incidental cleanup.
Moved down: a developer/researcher convenience tool with no existing breakage ranks below the wrapper bug fixes and the perf/unblocking work, despite its high per-PR score.

inconsistencies: Chain: #36105 (Windows exec fix) must be reviewed and merged before #36190, which only adds the functional tests for that behaviour; reviewing #36190 first is wasted effort.

#36105 and #36106 both fix the same binary (the bitcoin wrapper) in different ways and touch src/bitcoin.cpp / tool_bitcoin.py; coordinate them to avoid conflicting test changes — #36105 first since it re-enables the test on Windows that #36106 extends.
#19460 sits on top of #10102 and #29409 and only exists to unblock #19461; its own value is scaffolding, so it should not be reviewed ahead of its prerequisites.
#36603 is a stated prerequisite for #35054 (P2P UTXO set sharing); its band reflects that dependency, not just the bitcoin-util subcommand it adds.
#35814 supersedes the stalled #18606, #25243 and #30860 attempts at the same problem and depends on merged OpenRPC support (#34683) — the earlier attempts should be closed rather than reviewed.
#35994 is self-deprecated: the author prefers abandoning it in favour of manual rewrites, and the check introduced a witness-dropping bug; a close/redirect decision is more useful than a review.
#35831 changes ArgsManager parsing used by bitcoin-cli, bitcoin-wallet and bitcoin-tx, so it will interact with any wrapper/arg-handling changes in #36105/#36106; sequence them deliberately.
result.notes: The category is dominated by one genuine security fix (#36293) and a cluster of bitcoin-wrapper bugs; the remaining items are developer-convenience tools of broadly similar weight, so P3 is deliberately wide and ordered by how many people feel the problem (CLI users > fuzz/script developers > single-tool scaffolding).
